For we cannot find it in our hearts to number ourselves with or compare ourselves to those who praise themselves; but while they measure themselves by themselves and compare themselves with themselves, they understand nothing. But we will not rejoice beyond measure, but according to the size of the measure which God has distributed to us—a measure that reaches even to you. For we do not stretch ourselves beyond measure as though we had not reached you. For even to you have we come with the gospel of Christ, and we do not boast beyond measure in other men's labors; yes, and we hope, when your faith is increased among you, to be magnified according to our measure more largely, and to preach the gospel in those regions which are beyond you, and not to rejoice in what is already prepared by another man's measure. Let him who rejoices, rejoice in the Lord. For he who praises himself is not approved, but he whom the Lord praises.

# The epistle of Paul unto the Galatians.

### The first Chapter.

Paul, an Apostle—not of men, neither by man, but by Jesus Christ and by God the Father, who raised him from death—and all the brethren who are with me.

¶ Unto the congregation of Galatia.

¶ Grace be with you, and peace from God the Father and from our Lord Jesus Christ, who gave himself for our sins to deliver us from this present evil world, through the will of God our Father, to whom be praise for ever. Amen.

¶ I marvel that you are so soon turned from him that called you in the grace of Christ, unto another gospel—which is nothing else but that there are some who trouble you and intend to pervert the gospel of Christ. Nevertheless, though we ourselves or an angel from heaven preach any other gospel unto you than that which we have preached unto you, hold him as accursed. As I said before, so say I now again: if any man preach any other thing unto you than that you have received, hold him accursed. Do I now seek the favor of men, or of God?

<column-break/>

Or do I go about to please men? If I studied to please men, I would not be the servant of Christ.

¶ I certify to you, brethren, that the gospel which was preached by me was not after the manner of men; neither did I receive it of man, neither was I taught it, but received it by the revelation of Jesus Christ. You have heard of my conversation in times past in the Jewish ways: how that beyond measure I persecuted the congregation of God and spoiled it, and prevailed in the Jews' law above many of my companions who were of my own nation, and much more fervently maintained the traditions of the elders.

¶ But when it pleased God—who separated me from my mother's womb and called me by his grace to declare his Son through me, that I should preach him among the heathen—immediately I did not commune of the matter with flesh and blood, neither returned to Jerusalem to those who were Apostles before me, but went my way into Arabia and came again unto Damascus. Then after three years I returned to Jerusalem to Peter and stayed with him fifteen days. No other of the Apostles saw I, except James, the Lord's brother. The things which I write—behold, God knows I do not lie.

¶ After that I went into the coasts of Syria and Cilicia <note>The original text uses "Cicill," referring to the region of Cilicia.</note>, and was unknown in person to the congregations of Judea which were in Christ. But they heard only that he who persecuted us in time past now preaches the faith which he before destroyed. And they glorified God in me.

<summary>Paul opens his letter to the Galatians by asserting his divine calling as an apostle and rebuking the community for quickly abandoning the true gospel. He defends the divine origin of his message by recounting his transition from a persecutor of the church to a preacher, detailing his early travels to Arabia, Damascus, and Jerusalem.</summary>
<keywords>Paul, Galatians, Gospel, Apostle, Jesus Christ, Jerusalem, Peter, James, Damascus, conversion, Cilicia, Syria</keywords>

# ¶ The epistle of Paul.
## ¶ The second Chapter.

Then fourteen years after that, I went again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also. Yes, and I went by revelation and communed with them concerning the gospel which I preach among the Gentiles: but privately with those who are considered leaders, lest it should have been thought that I should run, or had run, in vain. Also Titus, who was with me, though he was a Greek, yet was not compelled to be circumcised; and that because of intruders who were false brothers, who came in among others to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage. To whom we gave no ground, no, not for the space of an hour, as concerning being brought into subjection; and that because the truth of the gospel might continue with you.

¶ From those who seem to be great (what they were in times past makes no difference to me: God respects no man's person); nevertheless, those who seem great added nothing to me. But on the contrary, when they saw that the gospel for the uncircumcised was committed to me, as the gospel for the circumcised was to Peter (for he who was mighty in Peter in the apostleship over the circumcised, the same was mighty in me among the Gentiles), and as soon as James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given to me, they gave to me and Barnabas their hands and agreed with us that

<column-break/>

we should preach among the heathen, and they among the Jews: warning only that we should remember the poor, which thing I was also diligent to do.

¶ When Peter had come to Antioch, I withstood him to his face, for he was worthy of blame. For before certain men came from James, he ate with the Gentiles; but when they had come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing those who were of the circumcision. And the other Jews dissembled likewise, so much that Barnabas was also brought into their hypocrisy. But when I saw that they did not go the right way according to the truth of the gospel, I said to Peter before all men: "If you, being a Jew, live after the manner of the Gentiles and not as the Jews do, why do you compel the Gentiles to follow the Jews?" We who are Jews by nature and not sinners of the Gentiles, know that a man is not justified by the deeds of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ; and we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ and not by the deeds of the law, because no flesh shall be justified by the deeds of the law.

¶ If, while we seek to be made righteous by Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, is Christ then the minister of sin? God forbid. For if I build again that which I destroyed, then I make myself a trespasser. But I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live for God. I am crucified with Christ. I live indeed, yet now not I, but Christ lives in me.

<summary>Paul recounts his meeting with the Jerusalem apostles, who endorsed his mission to the Gentiles, and describes his confrontation with Peter in Antioch regarding legalism. He argues that justification comes through faith in Christ rather than through adherence to the Jewish law.</summary>

The life which I now live in the flesh, I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me. I do not despise the grace of God: for if righteousness comes from the law, then Christ died in vain.

### The third Chapter.

O foolish Galatians: who has bewitched you, that you should not believe the truth? Before whose eyes Jesus Christ was clearly described and among you crucified? This only would I learn from you: did you receive the Spirit by the deeds of the law, or else by the preaching of faith? Are you so unwise that, after you have begun in the Spirit, you would now end in the flesh? Have you suffered so many things in vain? If it is so that you have suffered in vain. He who ministered the Spirit to you and works miracles among you, does he do it through the deeds of the law, or by the preaching of faith? Even as Abraham believed God, and it was ascribed to him for righteousness. Understand therefore, that those who are of faith are the children of Abraham.

¶ The scripture saw beforehand that God would justify the heathen through faith, and showed beforehand glad tidings to Abraham: "In you shall all nations be blessed." So then those who are of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham. For as many as are under the deeds of the law are under a curse. For it is written: cursed is every man who does not continue in all things which are written in the book of the law to fulfill them. That no man is justified by the law in the sight

¶ Brothers, I will speak after the manner of men: Though it is but a man's testament, yet no man despises it or adds anything to it when it is once approved. To Abraham and his seed were the promises made. He does not say, "in your seeds," as in many, but "in your seed," as in one, which is Christ. This I say: that the law, which began afterward, four hundred and thirty years later, does not annul the testament that was confirmed by God toward Christ, to make the promise of no effect. For if the inheritance comes from the law, it comes not from promise; but God gave it to Abraham by promise.

A mediator is not a mediator of one, but God is one. Is the law then against the promise of God? God forbid. ### The 6th Chapter.

Brethren, if any man be fallen by chance into any fault, you who are spiritual, help to amend him in the spirit of meekness; considering yourself, lest you also be tempted. Bear one another's burden, and so fulfill the law of Christ. If a man seems to himself to be something when indeed he is nothing, the same deceives himself in his imagination. Let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another. For every man shall bear his own burden.

Let him that is taught in the word minister to him that teaches him in all good things. Be not deceived; God is not mocked. For whatever a man sows, that shall he reap.

He that sows in the flesh shall of the flesh reap corruption; but he that sows in the spirit shall of the spirit reap life everlasting. Let us do good, and let us not faint. For when the time is come, we shall reap without weariness. While we have therefore time, let us do good to all men, and especially to those who are of the household of faith.

Behold how large a letter I have written to you with my own hand. As many as desire with outward appearance to please carnally, they constrain you to be circumcised, only because they would not suffer persecution for the cross of Christ. For they themselves who are circumcised do not keep the law; but desire to have you circumcised so that they might rejoice in your flesh. God forbid that I should rejoice except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, whereby the world is crucified as touching me, and I as concerning the world. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision avails anything at all, nor uncircumcision, but a new creature. And as many as walk according to this rule, peace be on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel that pertains to God. From henceforth let no man put me to trouble. For I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus. Brethren, the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.

Father and of Christ, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. This I say lest any man should beguile you with enticing words. For though I am absent in the flesh, yet am I present with you in the spirit, rejoicing and beholding the order that you keep, and your steadfast faith in Christ. As you have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, even so walk, rooted and built in him, and steadfast in the faith as you have learned; and therein be plenteous in giving thanks.

Beware lest any man come and spoil you through philosophy and deceitful vanity, through the traditions of men and ordinances after the world, and not after Christ. For in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily, and you are full in him, who is the head of all rule and power; in whom also you are circumcised with circumcision made without hands, by putting off the sinful body of the flesh through the circumcision that is in Christ. In that you are buried with him through baptism, in whom you are also risen again through faith that is wrought by the operation of God, who raised him from death.

And he has together with him quickened you also, who were dead in sin and in the uncircumcision of your flesh, and has forgiven us our trespasses, and has blotted out the obligation that was against us, made in the written law, and that he has taken out of the way and has fastened it to his cross, and has spoiled rule and power, and has made a show of them openly, and has triumphed over them in his own person.

Let no man therefore trouble your consciences

<column-break/>

about food and drink, or for a piece of a holy day, such as the holy day of the new moon or of the Sabbath day, which are nothing but shadows of things to come; but the body is in Christ. Let no man make you shoot at a wrong mark, who after his own imagination walks in the humbleness of angels—things which he never saw—causelessly puffed up with his fleshly mind, and does not hold the head, from which all the body, by joints and couples, receives nourishment, is knit together, and increases with the increasing that comes from God.

Wherefore, if you are dead with Christ from the doctrines of the world, why, as though you yet lived in the world, are you led with the traditions of those who say: "Touch not, taste not, handle not"? All of these perish with the using of them, and are according to the commandments and doctrines of men; which things have the appearance of wisdom in chosen holiness and humbleness, and in that they do not spare the body and give the flesh no honor regarding its needs.

Servants, be obedient unto your bodily masters in all things; not with eye-service as men-pleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing God. But he that does wrong shall receive for the wrong that he has done; for there is no respect of persons. You masters, do unto your servants that which is just and equal, remembering that you also have a master in heaven.

### ¶ The third Chapter.

Therefore, since we could no longer endure it, it pleased us to remain at Athens alone, and we sent Timothy, our brother and minister of God, and our fellow laborer in the gospel of Christ, to establish you and to comfort you concerning your faith, so that no man should be moved by these afflictions. For what thanks can we give to God in return for you, for all the joy with which we rejoice for your sakes before our God, while we night and day pray exceedingly that we might see you in person and might fulfill that which is lacking in your faith?

### The second Chapter.

WE beseech you, brothers, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and in that we shall assemble unto him, that you be not suddenly moved from your mind, and be not troubled, neither by spirit, nor by words, nor yet by letter which should seem to come from us, as though the day of Christ were at hand. Let no man deceive you by any means, for the Lord comes not except there come a departing first, and that that sinful man be revealed, the son of perdition, who is an adversary and is exalted above all that is called God or that is worshipped: so that he shall sit in the temple of God and show himself as God.

Remember you not, that when I was yet with you, I told you these things? And now you know what withholds: even that he might be

<column-break/>

revealed in his time. For already the mystery of iniquity works. Only he who holds, let him now hold until it be taken out of the way; and then shall that wicked one be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the appearance of his coming, even him whose coming is by the working of Satan, with all lying power, signs, and wonders: and in all deceivableness of unrighteousness among those who perish, because they have not received the love of the truth that they might have been saved. And therefore God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe lies: so that all they might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.

¶ We are bound to give thanks always to God for you, brothers beloved of the Lord, because God has from the beginning chosen you to salvation through the sanctifying of the Spirit and through believing the truth: whereunto he called you by our gospel, to obtain the glory that comes from our Lord Jesus Christ.

¶ Therefore, brothers, stand fast and keep the ordinances which you have learned: whether it was by our preaching or by our epistle. Our Lord Jesus Christ himself and God our Father, who has loved us and has given us everlasting consolation and good hope through grace, comfort your hearts and establish you in all saying and good doing.

## ¶ The 3rd Chapter.

Furthermore, brothers, pray for us, that the word of God may have free passage and be glorified, as it is with you; and that we may be delivered from unreasonable and evil men. For not all men have faith; but the Lord is faithful, who shall establish you and keep you from evil. We have confidence through the Lord toward you, that you both do and will do that which we command you. And the Lord guide your hearts into the love of God and the patience of Christ.

¶ We require you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you withdraw yourselves from every brother who walks disorderly and not after the instruction which you received from us. You yourselves know how you ought to imitate us: for we behaved not ourselves disorderly among you. Neither did we take bread from any man for nothing, but worked with labor and travel night and day, because we would not be burdensome to any of you; not because we did not have authority, but to make ourselves an example for you to imitate us. For when we were with you, we warned you of this: that if there were any who would not work, that the same should not eat.

¶ We have heard it said, no doubt, that there are some who walk among you disorderly and do not work at all, but are busybodies. Those who are such, we command and exhort in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that they work

<column-break/>

with quietness and eat their own bread. Brothers, be not weary in well-doing. If any man does not obey our word, send us word of him by a letter; and have no company with him, so that he may be ashamed. Yet do not count him as an enemy, but warn him as a brother.

¶ The very Lord of peace give you peace always, by all means. The Lord be with you all. The salutation of me, Paul, with my own hand. This is the token in all epistles. So I write. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with you all. Amen.

# The first epistle of Paul unto Timothy.
## The first Chapter.

Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the commandment of God our Savior, and of the Lord Jesus Christ, who is our hope.

To Timothy, his true son in the faith.

¶ Grace, mercy, and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ.

¶ As I urged you to remain still in Ephesus when I departed into Macedonia, even so do, that you may warn some that they teach no other doctrine; neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which breed doubts rather than godly edifying which is by faith. For the end of the commandment is love that comes from a pure heart, and from a good conscience, and from faith unfeigned. From which things some have erred and have turned unto vain talk, because they would be teachers of the scripture, and yet understand not what they speak, nor what they affirm.

¶ We know that the law is good, if a man uses it lawfully, understanding this: how the law is not given to a righteous man, but to the unrighteous and disobedient, to the ungodly and to

<column-break/>

synners, to the unholy and unclean, to murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers, to manslayers and whoremongers; to those who defile themselves with mankind; to kidnappers; to liars and to the perjured; and so forth, if there be any other thing that is contrary to wholesome doctrine according to the glorious gospel of the holy God, which gospel is committed to me.

¶ And I thank him who has made me strong in Christ Jesus our Lord; for he counted me faithful and put me into office, though before I was a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and a tyrant. Nevertheless, I obtained mercy because I did it ignorantly in unbelief; but the grace of our Lord was more abundant, with faith and love, which is in Christ Jesus.

¶ This is a true saying, and by all means worthy to be received, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am chief. Notwithstanding, mercy was given to me, so that Jesus Christ should first show in me all long-suffering, as an example to those who shall in time to come believe on him unto eternal life. So then, unto God, King everlasting, immortal, invisible, and only wise, be honor and praise for ever and ever. Amen.

¶ This commandment I commit to you, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which in time past were prophesied of you, that you by them should fight a good fight, having faith and a good conscience, which some have put away from them, and concerning faith have made shipwreck. Of whose number is

# Chapter 2.

I exhort therefore that, above all things, prayers, supplications, petitions, and giving of thanks be made for all men: for kings and for all who are in authority, so that we may live a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty. For that is good and accepted in the sight of God our Savior, who would have all men saved and come unto the knowledge of the truth. For there is one God and one mediator between God and man, which is the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all men, to be preached in due time; for which I am appointed a preacher and an apostle (I tell the truth in Christ and do not lie), being the teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.

¶ I will therefore that the men pray everywhere, lifting up pure hands without wrath or arguing. Likewise also the women, that they pray in modest apparel with shamefastness <note>modesty or humility</note> and honest behavior, not with braided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array; but with what becomes women who profess the worship of God through good works. Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. I do not allow a woman to teach, nor to have authority over a man, but to be in silence. For Adam was first formed, and 

<column-break/>

then Eve. Also, Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and was in transgression. Notwithstanding, they shall be saved through the bearing of children, if they continue in faith and in love and in holiness.

# Chapter 3.

This is a true saying: If a man desires the office of a bishop, he desires a good work. Indeed, a bishop must be blameless, the husband of one wife, sober, of honest behavior, modestly dressed, hospitable, apt to teach; not a drunkard, no fighter, not given to filthy lucre <note>dishonest financial gain</note>, but gentle, abhorring fighting, abhorring covetousness, and one who rules his own house honestly, having children under obedience with all honesty. For if a man cannot rule his own house, how shall he care for the congregation of God? He must not be a new convert <note>literally "a young man"</note>, lest he swell with pride and fall into the judgment of the evil speaker <note>the slanderer or the devil</note>. He must also be well reported of among those who are outside <note>non-believers</note>, lest he fall into rebuke and into the snare of the evil speaker.

¶ Likewise, the deacons must be honest, not double-tongued, not given to much drinking, nor to filthy lucre, but holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. And let them first be proved, and then let them minister, if they be found blameless.

¶ Even so must their wives be honest, not evil speakers, but sober and faithful in all things.

### Chapter 4.

The Spirit speaks clearly that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith and shall give heed to spirits of error and devilish doctrine of those who speak falsely through hypocrisy, having their consciences marked with a hot iron, forbidding to marry and commanding to abstain from foods which God has created to be received with thanksgiving by those who believe and have known the truth. For all the creatures of God are good, and nothing is to be refused if it is received with thanksgiving; for it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer. If you shall put the brethren in remembrance of these things, you shall be a good minister of Jesus Christ,

<column-break/>

having been nourished up in the words of faith and good doctrine, which doctrine you have continually followed. But cast away ungodly and old wives' fables.

¶ Exercise yourself unto godliness. For bodily exercise profits little, but godliness is good for all things, as a thing which has promises of the life that is now and of the life to come. This is a sure saying and by all parties worthy to be received. For therefore we labor and suffer rebuke, because we believe in the living God, who is the Savior of all men, but especially of those who believe. Command and teach such things. Let no man despise your youth, but be an example to those who believe, in word, in conversation <note>conduct or lifestyle</note>, in love, in spirit, in faith, and in purity.

¶ Until I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, and to doctrine. Do not despise the gift that is in you, which was given to you through prophecy and with the laying on of the hands of a senior <note>an elder or presbyter</note>. Exercise these things and give yourself to them, so that all men may see how you profit. Take heed to yourself and to learning, and continue in them. For if you shall do so, you shall save yourself and those who hear you.

¶ Honor true widows. If any widow has children or grandchildren, let them learn first to rule their own houses godly and to repay their parents. For that is good and acceptable before God. She who is a true widow and friendless puts her trust in God and continues in supplication and prayer night and day; but she who lives in pleasure is dead even while she is alive. And command these things, so that they may be without fault. If there is anyone who does not provide for his own, and especially for those of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.

¶ Let no widow be chosen under sixty years old, and such a one who was the wife of one man and well reported of for good works: if she has brought up children, if she has been generous to strangers, if she has washed the saints' feet, if she has helped those who were in adversity, if she was continually given to every kind of good work. Refuse the younger widows. For when they have begun to grow wanton against Christ, then they will marry, having condemnation because they have cast off their first faith. And also they learn to go from house to house idle—and not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, speaking things which are not proper.

¶ I will therefore that the younger women marry, bear children, and manage the house, giving no occasion to the adversary to speak evil. For many of them have already turned back and have gone after Satan. And if any man or woman

Teach and exhort these things. If any man teaches otherwise and is not content with the wholesome words of the Lord Jesus Christ and with the doctrine of godliness, he is puffed up and knows nothing: but wastes his brain about questions and strife over words, from which spring envy, strife, railings, evil suspicions, and pointless disputes in the schools of men with corrupt minds and destitute of the truth, who think that lucre is godliness. Separate yourself from such people. 

Godliness is great riches if a man is content with what he has. For we brought nothing into the world, and it is a plain case that we can carry nothing out. When we have food and clothing, let us be content with them. Those who want to be rich fall into temptation and snares, and into many foolish and harmful lusts which drown men in perdition and destruction. For covetousness is the root of all evil; which while some lusted after, they erred from the faith and entangled themselves with many sorrows. 

But you, who are the man of God, flee such things. Follow righteousness, godliness, love, patience, and meekness. Fight the good fight of faith. Lay hand on eternal life, to which you are called and have made a good profession before many witnesses. I give you charge in the sight of God, who gives life to all things, and before Jesus Christ

who witnessed a good confession under Pontius Pilate, that you keep the commandment without spot, so that no man finds fault with you, until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ; which appearing (when the time has come) He shall show, who is blessed and the only Mighty, King of kings and Lord of lords, who alone has immortality and dwells in light that no man can attain, whom no man has seen nor can see: to whom be honor and everlasting rule. Amen.

Command those who are rich in this world that they not be overly wise, and that they do not trust in uncertain riches but in the living God, who gives us all things abundantly to enjoy them; and that they do good and be rich in good works, ready to give and to distribute, laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, so that they may obtain eternal life. 

O Timothy, guard that which is given to you to keep, and avoid unholy vanities of voices and oppositions of <term>science</term> <note>In this context, knowledge or "gnosis".</note> falsely so called; which science, while some professed it, they have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with you. Amen.

# ¶ The second epistle of
## ¶ Paul To Timothy

### ¶ The first Chapter.

Paul, an Apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, to preach the promise of life, which life is in Christ Jesus. To Timothy, his beloved son: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from Jesus Christ our Lord.

¶ I thank God, whom I serve as my ancestors did with a pure conscience, that without ceasing I make mention of you in my prayers night and day, desiring to see you, being mindful of your tears, so that I may be filled with joy when I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in you, which dwelt first in your grandmother Lois and in your mother Eunice; and I am assured that it dwells in you also.

¶ Therefore I remind you that you stir up the gift of God which is in you by the laying on of my hands. For God has not given us the spirit of fear, but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind <note>The original "honest behaveour" refers to the Greek *sophronismos*, meaning self-control or a sound mind.</note>. Do not be ashamed to testify of our Lord, nor be ashamed of me, who am a prisoner for his sake; but suffer adversity with the gospel also through the power of God, who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our deeds, but for his own purpose

<column-break/>

and grace, which grace was given to us through Christ Jesus before the world began, but is now declared openly by the appearing of our Savior Jesus Christ, who has abolished death and has brought life and immortality to light through the gospel, for which I am appointed a preacher, and an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles. For this reason, I also suffer these things. Nevertheless, I am not ashamed. For I know whom I have believed, and am sure that he is able to keep that which I have committed to his keeping against that day.

¶ See that you hold fast the example of the wholesome words which you heard from me, in faith and love which is in Jesus Christ. That good thing which was committed to your keeping, keep by the Holy Spirit who dwells in us. This you know, that all those who are in Asia have turned away from me, among whom are Phigellus and Hermogenes. The Lord give mercy to the house of Onesiphorus, for he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of my chain; but when he was in Rome, he sought me out very diligently and found me. The Lord grant to him that he may find mercy with the Lord on that day. And in how many things he ministered to me at Ephesus, you know very well.

You therefore, my son, be strong in the grace that is in Christ Jesus. And what things you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same to faithful men, who

¶ Despisers of those who are good, traitors, headstrong, high-minded, lovers of pleasure more than lovers of God, having a semblance of godly living, but they have denied the power of it. Abhor such people. For of this sort are those who enter into houses and lead into bondage women laden with sin, which women are led by various lusts, always learning, and never able to come unto the knowledge of the truth.

¶ Just as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, even so do these resist the truth; they are men of corrupt minds and reprobate concerning the faith. But they shall prevail no longer, for their madness shall be manifest unto all men, as theirs was. But you have seen the experience of my doctrine, manner of life, purpose, faith, longsuffering, love, patience, persecutions, and afflictions which happened unto me at Antioch, at Iconium, and at Lystra—which persecutions I suffered patiently, and from them all the Lord delivered me. Yes, and all who will live godly in Christ Jesus must suffer persecutions. But evil men and deceivers shall grow worse and worse, while they deceive and are deceived themselves.

¶ But continue in the things which you have learned, which also were committed unto you, seeing you know from whom you have learned them, and because also from a child you have known the holy scripture, which is able to make you wise unto salvation <note>The original "health" refers to spiritual health or salvation.</note> through faith which is in Christ Jesus. For all scripture given by inspiration of God is profitable to teach, to reprove,

<column-break/>

<header>unto Timothy. fo. cclxxxvij</header>

to inform, and to instruct in righteousness, that the man of God may be perfect and prepared unto all good works.

### The 4th Chapter.

¶ I testify therefore before God and before the Lord Jesus Christ, who shall judge the living and the dead at his appearing in his kingdom: preach the word; be fervent, whether it is in season or out of season. Reprove, rebuke, exhort with all longsuffering. For the time will come when they will not suffer wholesome doctrine; but according to their own lusts shall they (whose ears itch) gather to themselves a heap of teachers, and shall turn their ears from the truth and shall be given unto fables. But you watch in all things, and suffer adversity, and do the work of an evangelist; fulfill your office to the utmost.

¶ For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departing is at hand. I have fought a good fight, and I have finished my course, and I have kept the faith. From henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, who is a righteous judge, shall give me at that day—not to me only, but unto all those who love his coming. Make haste to come unto me at once.

¶ For Demas has left me and has loved this present world, and has departed into Thessalonica. Crescens is gone to Galatia, and Titus unto Dalmatia. Only Luke is with me. Take Mark and bring him with you, for he is necessary unto me for ministry. And Tichicus I have sent to Ephesus. The cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus,

# The second epistle of Paul.

When you come, bring with you the books—but especially the parchments. Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil; the Lord reward him according to his deeds. You should also beware of him, for he strongly withstood our preaching.

¶ At my first defense of myself, no man assisted me, but all forsook me. I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge. Notwithstanding, the Lord assisted me and strengthened me, so that through me the preaching might be fulfilled to the utmost and that all the Gentiles might hear. And I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion. And the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work and shall keep me until his heavenly kingdom. To whom be praise for ever and ever, Amen.

¶ Greet Prisca and Aquila, and the household of Onesiphorus. Erastus stayed at Corinth. Trophimus I left sick at Miletus. Make haste to come before winter. Eubulus greets you, as do Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brethren. The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit.

¶ Grace be with you, Amen.

The second epistle written from Rome to Timothy, when Paul was presented the second time before the Emperor Nero.

# The epistle of Paul unto Titus.

## The first Chapter.

<image-desc>Intricate woodcut drop cap 'P' set within an architectural frame featuring an archway and decorative foliage.</image-desc>Paul, the servant of God and an Apostle of Jesus Christ, to preach the faith of God's elect and the knowledge of the truth—which truth is in serving God in hope of eternal life, which life God (who cannot lie) promised before the world began; but has at the appointed time opened his word by preaching, which preaching is committed unto me by the commandment of God our Savior.

¶ To Titus, his natural son in the common faith.

¶ Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ our Savior.

¶ For this cause I left you in Crete, that you should perform that which was lacking and should ordain elders <note>The original "seniours" refers to church elders or presbyters.</note> in every city, as I appointed you. If any be such as no man can complain about—the husband of one wife, having faithful children who are not slandered for riotous living or disobedience. For a bishop must be such as no man can complain about, as it becomes the minister of God: not stubborn, not angry, no drunkard, no fighter, not given

¶ For there are many who are disobedient, vain talkers, and deceivers of minds, especially those of the circumcision, whose mouths must be stopped, who pervert whole houses, teaching things which they ought not for the sake of dishonest gain. One of them, who was a poet of their own, said: "The Cretians are always liars, evil beasts, and lazy gluttons." This testimony is true; therefore, rebuke them sharply, so that they may be sound in the faith and not pay attention to Jewish fables and the commandments of men who turn away from the truth. Unto the pure, all things are pure: but unto those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but even their very minds and consciences are defiled. They profess that they know God, but with their deeds they deny him, being abominable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.

### ¶ The Second Chapter. ¶

But speak you that which becomes wholesome learning: That the older men be sober, honest, discreet, sound in the faith, in love, and in patience. And the elder women likewise, that they be in such clothing as becomes holiness, not false accusers, not given to much drink,

<column-break/>

<header>Unto Titus.</header>

but teachers of honest things, that they may train the young women to love their husbands, to love their children, to be of honest behavior, chaste, housewifely, good, and obedient to their own husbands, so that the word of God is not evil spoken of. Exhort young men likewise that they be of honest manners.

¶ Above all things, show yourself as an example of good works in the doctrine; show integrity, honesty, and the wholesome word which cannot be rebuked, so that he who opposes you may be ashamed, having nothing in you that he may dispraise. Exhort servants to be obedient to their own masters and to please them in all things, not answering back, nor being pilferers, but showing all good faithfulness, so that they may bring honor to the doctrine of God our Savior in all things. For the grace of God, which brings salvation to all men, has appeared and teaches us that we should deny ungodliness and worldly lusts, and that we should live honestly, righteously, and godly in this present world, looking for that blessed hope and glorious appearing of the mighty God and of our Savior Jesus Christ, who gave himself for us to redeem us from all unrighteousness and to purify for himself a special people, fervently devoted to good works. Speak these things, and exhort, and rebuke with all authority. See that no man despises you.

Speak evil of no man, that they be no fighters, but gentle, showing all meekness unto all men. For we ourselves also were in times past unwise, disobedient, deceived, subject to lusts and to various manners of pleasure, living in malice and envy, full of hate, and hating one another.
¶ But after the kindness and love of our Savior toward man appeared—not because of the deeds of righteousness which we wrought, but because of his mercy—he saved us, by the fountain of the new birth and with the renewing of the Holy Ghost, which he shed on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior; that we, once justified by his grace, should be heirs of eternal life through hope. This is a true saying.
¶ Of these things I would have you affirm, so that those who believe in God might be diligent to go forward in good works. These things are good and profitable unto men. Foolish questions, and genealogies, and brawling and strife about the law, avoid; for they are unprofitable and superfluous. A man who is the author of sects, after the first and the second warning, avoid, remembering that he who is such a person is perverted and sins, even condemned by his own judgment.
¶ When I shall send Artemas unto you, or Tychicus, be diligent to come to me at Nicopolis, for I have determined to winter there. Bring Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey diligently, so that nothing is lacking to them. And let ours also learn to excel in good

<column-break/>

works as far as necessity requires, so that they be not unfruitful. All who are with me salute you. Greet those who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all, Amen.
